From: Ethan Jacobson <ethan.jacobson@insurity.com>
Subject: Refine daemon bug

Body:
## Summary
  The workflow runner-worker loop stops making progress after it fails to durably settle a
  stale-candidate integration, yet its OS process stays alive. Once wedged, the daemon admits
  no new work (Todo Goals never reach Plan), stops reaping agents past their hard cap, and
  stops cleaning worktrees �X indefinitely, until a manual daemon restart. Nothing detects or
  surfaces the dead loop: `refine next` reports "all-quiet" and `system status` reports
  daemon_healthy=true with running_workflow_processes=0.

  ## Field evidence (Refine 4.2.0, node bo2lnxnevo02-ethan, daemon port 8082)
  - Last log entry of ANY kind: 2026-08-18T21:50:00Z (category=workflow):
    "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded); original error:
     Candidate 11818bcf�K is stale: recorded base 2a4dccff�K is not <current>".
    Preceding lines show repeated "Candidate �K is stale" / "! [rejected] �K non-fast-forward"
    while integrating round branches during concurrent activity on merge_target_branch
    `insurity-claims`.
  - ~44h later: zero subsequent log lines. No "Workflow status changed" since 08-18T21:48.
  - A Goal created + started today sits in `todo` and is never admitted to `plan`.
  - system status: daemon_healthy=true, running_workflow_processes=0,
    parallel_run_cap=2 (capacity free). refine next: suggestion "all-quiet".
  - State-sync is healthy (sync_recovered 2026-08-18T13:48; `sync --preview` fast-forwards;
    origin push of refine/state succeeded today) �X so sync is NOT the blocker.
  - Collateral from the stalled loop: 3 agent sessions alive 21�V27h, far past
    agent_hard_cap_seconds=7200 and agent_idle_timeout_seconds=900, unreaped; 7 orphaned
    worktrees under .git/refine-worktrees not cleaned. This indicates the SAME loop that
    admits work also owns reaping/cleanup, and all of it stopped together.
  - Restarting the daemon respawns the worker and immediately resumes admission, reaping,
    and cleanup.

  ## Root-cause hypothesis (confirm in code)
  The "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded)" path �X reached when a
  candidate's recorded base is stale and the failure record is superseded by a concurrent
  attempt �X is not handled as a recoverable per-Goal outcome. Instead of logging the failure
  and continuing the loop to the next Goal, the worker's main loop exits or deadlocks (e.g.
  an error propagates out of the loop body, an await never completes, or a lock/worktree is
  left held). The supervisor keeps the process alive (so `system status` looks healthy) but
  the loop no longer ticks.

  Start in the workflow runner-worker entrypoint (`refine system runner-worker --kind
  workflow`) and the engine loop under src/application/workflow/engine/execution/. Find where
  "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded)" and the stale-candidate error
  ("Candidate �K is stale: recorded base �K") are produced, and trace what happens to the loop
  after that error �X specifically whether the error escapes the per-Goal iteration boundary.

  ## Required behavior
  1. A per-Goal failure �X including "attempt superseded" / stale-candidate / non-fast-forward
     push rejection �X must be caught at the per-Goal boundary, recorded durably (Goal ->
     failed or a recovery Round), and the worker loop MUST continue to the next Goal. No
     single-Goal integration failure may terminate or wedge the loop.
  2. Liveness detection: the worker must emit a periodic heartbeat/tick, and the daemon must
     detect a stalled loop (alive process, no progress/heartbeat within a bound) and either
     auto-restart the worker or mark itself unhealthy. system status must report a wedged
     worker as NOT healthy.
  3. Observability: when a Todo Goal has been waiting past a threshold with free capacity and
     no active runs, `refine next` must surface it (e.g. "workflow worker not advancing:
     last tick <ts>, N Goals stuck in todo") with a remediation command, instead of
     "all-quiet".
  4. Decouple or make independently resilient the periodic duties driven by this loop
     (admission, agent hard-cap/idle reaping, worktree cleanup) so one wedged concern does
     not silently stop the others.

  ## Reproduction
  1. Start a Goal whose implementation round races the merge_target_branch so its candidate
     goes stale on integration (recorded base no longer current), and arrange a concurrent
     attempt so the failure is "superseded" and cannot be durably settled.
  2. Observe the worker log the "attempt superseded" line and then stop ticking.
  3. Create + start another Goal; it stays in `todo` and is never admitted; refine next says
     "all-quiet"; running_workflow_processes stays 0; agents past hard cap go unreaped.
  4. Restart the daemon �� admission/reaping/cleanup resume. Confirms the loop, not the data,
     was the blocker.

  ## Acceptance criteria
  - A stale-candidate / superseded-attempt integration failure records the Goal outcome and
    the worker continues to the next Goal WITHOUT wedging; a follow-up Todo Goal is admitted
    to Plan within one poll interval.
  - A wedged/stalled worker loop is detected (heartbeat/tick watchdog) and auto-recovered or
    reported unhealthy in system status �X no manual restart required.
  - refine next surfaces a stuck-Todo-with-idle-worker condition instead of "all-quiet".
  - Reaper and worktree-cleanup keep running independent of an admission-path failure.
  - Regression tests (style of src/application/workflow/tests/ and
    src/infrastructure/process/supervisor/lifecycle/tests.rs): inject a superseded/stale
    candidate failure and assert the loop survives and the next Goal is admitted; assert the
    watchdog flags a non-ticking worker.

  ## Constraints
  - Preserve fail-closed safety for genuine content conflicts and never auto-merge contested
    Goal records; this fix is about loop survival, liveness detection, and surfacing �X not
    about weakening conflict handling.

From: Ethan Jacobson <ethan.jacobson@insurity.com>
Subject: Refine daemon bug

Body:
## Summary
  The workflow runner-worker loop stops making progress after it fails to durably settle a
  stale-candidate integration, yet its OS process stays alive. Once wedged, the daemon admits
  no new work (Todo Goals never reach Plan), stops reaping agents past their hard cap, and
  stops cleaning worktrees �X indefinitely, until a manual daemon restart. Nothing detects or
  surfaces the dead loop: `refine next` reports "all-quiet" and `system status` reports
  daemon_healthy=true with running_workflow_processes=0.

  ## Field evidence (Refine 4.2.0, node bo2lnxnevo02-ethan, daemon port 8082)
  - Last log entry of ANY kind: 2026-08-18T21:50:00Z (category=workflow):
    "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded); original error:
     Candidate 11818bcf�K is stale: recorded base 2a4dccff�K is not <current>".
    Preceding lines show repeated "Candidate �K is stale" / "! [rejected] �K non-fast-forward"
    while integrating round branches during concurrent activity on merge_target_branch
    `insurity-claims`.
  - ~44h later: zero subsequent log lines. No "Workflow status changed" since 08-18T21:48.
  - A Goal created + started today sits in `todo` and is never admitted to `plan`.
  - system status: daemon_healthy=true, running_workflow_processes=0,
    parallel_run_cap=2 (capacity free). refine next: suggestion "all-quiet".
  - State-sync is healthy (sync_recovered 2026-08-18T13:48; `sync --preview` fast-forwards;
    origin push of refine/state succeeded today) �X so sync is NOT the blocker.
  - Collateral from the stalled loop: 3 agent sessions alive 21�V27h, far past
    agent_hard_cap_seconds=7200 and agent_idle_timeout_seconds=900, unreaped; 7 orphaned
    worktrees under .git/refine-worktrees not cleaned. This indicates the SAME loop that
    admits work also owns reaping/cleanup, and all of it stopped together.
  - Restarting the daemon respawns the worker and immediately resumes admission, reaping,
    and cleanup.

  ## Root-cause hypothesis (confirm in code)
  The "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded)" path �X reached when a
  candidate's recorded base is stale and the failure record is superseded by a concurrent
  attempt �X is not handled as a recoverable per-Goal outcome. Instead of logging the failure
  and continuing the loop to the next Goal, the worker's main loop exits or deadlocks (e.g.
  an error propagates out of the loop body, an await never completes, or a lock/worktree is
  left held). The supervisor keeps the process alive (so `system status` looks healthy) but
  the loop no longer ticks.

  Start in the workflow runner-worker entrypoint (`refine system runner-worker --kind
  workflow`) and the engine loop under src/application/workflow/engine/execution/. Find where
  "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded)" and the stale-candidate error
  ("Candidate �K is stale: recorded base �K") are produced, and trace what happens to the loop
  after that error �X specifically whether the error escapes the per-Goal iteration boundary.

  ## Required behavior
  1. A per-Goal failure �X including "attempt superseded" / stale-candidate / non-fast-forward
     push rejection �X must be caught at the per-Goal boundary, recorded durably (Goal ->
     failed or a recovery Round), and the worker loop MUST continue to the next Goal. No
     single-Goal integration failure may terminate or wedge the loop.
  2. Liveness detection: the worker must emit a periodic heartbeat/tick, and the daemon must
     detect a stalled loop (alive process, no progress/heartbeat within a bound) and either
     auto-restart the worker or mark itself unhealthy. system status must report a wedged
     worker as NOT healthy.
  3. Observability: when a Todo Goal has been waiting past a threshold with free capacity and
     no active runs, `refine next` must surface it (e.g. "workflow worker not advancing:
     last tick <ts>, N Goals stuck in todo") with a remediation command, instead of
     "all-quiet".
  4. Decouple or make independently resilient the periodic duties driven by this loop
     (admission, agent hard-cap/idle reaping, worktree cleanup) so one wedged concern does
     not silently stop the others.

  ## Reproduction
  1. Start a Goal whose implementation round races the merge_target_branch so its candidate
     goes stale on integration (recorded base no longer current), and arrange a concurrent
     attempt so the failure is "superseded" and cannot be durably settled.
  2. Observe the worker log the "attempt superseded" line and then stop ticking.
  3. Create + start another Goal; it stays in `todo` and is never admitted; refine next says
     "all-quiet"; running_workflow_processes stays 0; agents past hard cap go unreaped.
  4. Restart the daemon �� admission/reaping/cleanup resume. Confirms the loop, not the data,
     was the blocker.

  ## Acceptance criteria

skill.prompt:
## Governance review

Review the exact candidate against the project's stated intent and attached Skills. Read the accepted plans, implementation and Quality evidence and actual diff. Report actual violations with evidence, not hypothetical risks or preferences. Do not edit files, merge, push or change Goal state. A finding must identify the violated intent or invariant, its concrete consequence, and an actionable recovery request. Group related symptoms by their underlying cause; an alternative design preference alone is not a violation.

## Product intent

Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

## Project rules

- Keep domain concepts, invariants, and pure policy in `src/model`; shared behavior and orchestration in `src/application`; Git, process, host, storage, provider, and telemetry mechanisms in `src/infrastructure`; and adapters for people and machines in `src/surfaces`. Keep `error.rs` as a neutral shared boundary. Model remains independent of the other areas, and code outside Surfaces does not depend on surface adapters.
- Maintain a consistent architecture by extending the existing semantic responsibilities and dependency boundaries described in `docs/intent/01-design.md`. Prefer existing concepts and shared owners. A new or refined domain concept is appropriate when it explains the required behavior and reduces duplicated policy or special cases while preserving those boundaries.
- Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching. Keep CLI and API work under 50 ms, excluding time spent waiting on LLMs or outside tools.
- Maintain affected documentation, especially `docs/intent/*`, and preserve its established format. Apply the scope limits in the intent guidance below.
- Keep Refine agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate or reimplement coding-agent functionality.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
